subject: System Design
title: The Anatomy of a Web Request
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Anatomy of a Web Request usable.

hook.text: You type a URL and press Enter. In 300 milliseconds, a page appears. What happened in between?

buildup.text: DNS resolves the domain. Your browser opens a TCP connection and sends an HTTP request.

discovery.text: A load balancer routes you to one of many servers. The server queries a database and returns HTML.

twist.text: CDN caches, TLS handshakes, and connection pooling all happen invisibly to make it feel instant.

climax.text: A single web request touches DNS, load balancers, servers, databases, and caches — in milliseconds.

punchline.text: One click triggers a dozen systems in 300ms.

quiz.question: What is the first step when you type a URL?
options: DNS resolves the domain name to an IP address
